## Context / Problem
Completion verification currently materializes the full Git-backed ticket store although a run reads only a small subset. Close traces attributed 135-235 seconds to this phase. Approved research on `shaven-censorable-sifaka` measured the real store: tracker-OID capture was 9.5 ms p50, tree/object reads about 11 ms p50, and fetching plus uncached reduction of one real ticket was 29.156 ms for 10 files / 62,426 bytes with exact state-hash parity. Revision A stayed byte-identical after a normal rebar write advanced the live tracker to B.

The close path also publishes PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT`, closing `STATUS`, and completion `SIGNATURE` through separate writes. A durable PASS can outlive a failed close, and a closed ticket can outlive a failed signature. We need one stable read basis and one atomic publication boundary.

## Contract
- `code_oid` is resolved once from `--ref`; `tickets_oid` independently identifies tracker state. Typed interfaces must prevent swapping them.
- The ticket view reads Git objects lazily at `tickets_oid`, never falls back to live state, and never writes caches inside the view.
- The read receipt records exact tickets, negative reads, direct-child membership, transitive descendants, inbound/outbound relations and consulted reachability, plus global resolver inputs such as `.bridge_state/bindings.json`.
- Atomic means one committed-store transaction contains PASS sidecar, closed STATUS, and completion SIGNATURE, or none is committed and HEAD/index/worktree return to their prior state. OID-pinned readers see the complete old or complete new commit.

## Plan
1. Add a pinned-ticket reader backed by `ls-tree`, batched `cat-file`, and the existing uncached reducer input seam. Resolve arbitrary IDs/aliases/Jira bindings at `tickets_oid`; record not-found as a negative read. Put derived resolver/graph indexes outside the immutable tree and key them by tracker OID plus schema version. Unsupported broad queries fail closed.
2. Thread this view through completion context assembly, deterministic ticket checks, and agent ticket tools. Keep code reads on the separate code snapshot. Bug `shimmery-customary-dorking` will experimentally test the suspected live-code gap; this story preserves typed separation without assuming that hypothesis is true.
3. Before mutation, validate the receipt from A against current descendant Tn. Reject non-ancestor history. Diff changed ticket/global paths and recompute affected predicates at both endpoints. Unrelated changes may continue; an exact, hierarchy, link, negative, or resolver conflict discards the verdict and restarts at Tn.
4. Outside the write lock, prepare the verdict, receipt digest, completion certificate payload, event UUIDs, and all work not requiring final HLC order. Each run owns `(run_id, code_oid, tickets_oid, receipt_digest)` and unique temporary paths.
5. Extend the status transaction to accept three prepared close events. Inside the lock, assert tracker HEAD still equals validated Tn and root status remains `in_progress`; finalize HLC/parent linkage/authorship, stage all three, and make one local Git commit. Any signing, staging, index, or commit fault rolls back only this bundle and restores pre-operation state. Preserve reducer/event compatibility.
6. Release the lock before ordinary fast-forward push. On rejection, fetch and revalidate: rebuild/retry an unrelated delta or restart verification for a relevant delta. Never force a ref update or push. A same-ticket race is idempotent only when the existing close binds an equivalent code OID, receipt, and attestation; a loser leaves no PASS sidecar.
7. Measure ticket-OID capture, lazy reads/reduction, receipt validation, bundle preparation, lock wait/hold, local commit, and push/retry. Metrics add only constant-time timestamps inside the lock. Document the receipt vocabulary, atomicity boundary, retries, rollout, and separate code/ticket revisions.

## Rollout / Back-out
Put the new completion path behind one configuration switch and retain the legacy path as an explicit operator back-out during dogfooding. Selection is fixed and recorded at operation start; a run never silently falls back after capturing `tickets_oid`. Default enablement is separate and evidence-based. The mechanism is in-process and CI-provider-independent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Given tracker A and later normal write B, a run pinned to A returns byte/state-identical ticket reads while live writes continue, without materializing the full ticket tree.
- [x] Any ticket requested at runtime loads from A and extends the receipt; missing returns not-found-at-A plus a negative dependency, never live fallback.
- [x] Direct/transitive hierarchy and inbound/outbound relation predicates invalidate on relevant create/remove/reparent/relink changes; a proven unrelated mutation remains valid.
- [x] Alias/Jira/global binding resolution is pinned to A; relevant binding changes invalidate. Unsupported queries fail closed.
- [x] Completion code evidence remains bound to separately resolved `code_oid`; tests reject swapped code/ticket roots.
- [x] LLM work, lazy reads, receipt validation, preparation, and push occur outside the write lock. Only final HEAD/status assertions, ordering/signing, staging, and one commit are inside; wait/hold are measured.
- [x] A successful close creates exactly one local commit containing PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT`, `STATUS in_progress -> closed`, and completion `SIGNATURE`, all bound to one run/code/receipt identity.
- [x] Fault injection at signing, staging, index, and commit boundaries leaves prior HEAD/status and no committed sidecar/signature; retry creates at most one equivalent bundle.
- [x] Two parallel reviews cannot publish mixed artifacts: one wins; the loser recognizes an equivalent close or restarts without leaving PASS. Unrelated reviews may both commit after revalidation.
- [x] Non-ancestor state, relevant receipt drift, and remote fast-forward rejection fail closed without force; unrelated descendant deltas can revalidate/retry.
- [x] Derived caches are OID/schema-keyed with per-run temporaries and do not write inside the pinned view.
- [x] Focused lazy-read parity, hierarchy/link phantom, negative-read, resolver, cross-process concurrency, and rollback tests pass in CI, followed by project lint, typecheck, and test gates.
- [x] Documentation covers the stable-read contract, full receipt vocabulary, committed-store atomicity, rollout/back-out, remote-writer limitation, and metric phases.

## Out of Scope
- Replacing Git or reducing the lock to `git update-ref` while the mutable checkout remains authoritative.
- Acting on either unproven bug (`shimmery-customary-dorking`, `lineny-barathea-ladybug`) before its experiment.
- Setting a lock-duration SLO before instrumentation produces a distribution.
